subject: POC measurement playbook and acceptance targets (Lumina Health)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@luminahealth.com>; Adam Jenkins <adam.jenkins@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: POC measurement playbook and acceptance targets (Lumina Health)

Thanks again for the time today — good alignment on the high-level use case and success criteria. Below is a concise post-call recap and a proposed evaluation plan so both sides can sign off and move to a short POC. If this looks good I’ll schedule a kickoff (target week of 7/19).

1) Primary goal: validate that Redwood can run the Lumina triage/inference workload at 95th-percentile latency and cost targets while maintaining quality on your sample cases.

2) Acceptance targets (proposed):
   - Latency: 95th-pctl <= 150 ms for inference requests with median sequence length ~120 tokens (99th pctl fallback plan documented).
   - Throughput: sustain ~120 concurrent requests (approx. 40 r/s peak per model shard) with <1% error rate over a 1-hour soak.
   - Cost: amortized inference cost <= $0.0015 per token at trial-scale workload (batching + KV cache applied).
   - Quality: top-intent match >= 92% on the labeled validation set; hallucination rate <2% across sampled prompts.

3) Evaluation plan (2-week trial):
   - Phase A (days 1–3): onboarding, dataset ingest, baseline smoke test. Redwood provides sandbox endpoint + access to an instrumentation dashboard.
   - Phase B (days 4–10): run deterministic test suite + randomized workload from "workload-sample.jsonl" (attached). Collect latency, success/error codes, token counts, and model outputs for quality scoring.
   - Phase C (days 11–14): run 1-hour soak at peak concurrency, final readout, and decision meeting.

4) Ownership and roles:
   - Lumina: Sara Liu (DS lead) — provide labeled validation set, confirm top-intent mapping; Adam Jenkins — infra contact for network/VPC access.
   - Redwood: Karthik Iyer — trial owner and primary contact; Monica Patel — deployment and ops; Ben Carter — success criteria / CS on quality measurement.

5) Data / security notes: sanitized PII only for the trial; we’ll use our private ingestion path and audit logging. If Lumina needs a VPC peering option we can scope it as a short add-on.

6) Next steps (please confirm by EOD):
   - Lumina: confirm acceptance targets above and share a small labeled validation set (<= 3k examples)
   - Redwood: deliver sandbox credentials, attach initial poc-playbook-v1.pdf and workload-sample.jsonl, schedule 30-minute kickoff for 7/20 or 7/21.

Regards,
Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC measurement playbook and acceptance targets (Lumina Health)

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful and matches the internal readout I emailed to Adam. A few clarifications from our side before sign-off: 

- Latency: the 150 ms 95th target is aggressive but reasonable — could you add the target for cold-starts / 99th pctl so we can show it to infra?
- Cost: we’ll validate the $0.0015/token projection during the run; can you share the assumptions (batch size, typical seq length distribution) used to estimate that?
- Quality: our labeled set is roughly 2,100 examples; we’ll sanitize and upload by Friday (7/16).

If you can add a short appendix in the playbook with the cost assumptions and the soak plan (1-hour vs 30-minute), we can confirm and be ready for a 7/20 kickoff.

Sara Liu
Principal Data Scientist, Lumina Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: POC measurement playbook and acceptance targets (Lumina Health)

Sara — thanks. We’ve updated the playbook (attached) with the cost assumptions and soak options. Short answers here: 

- Cold-starts / 99th pctl: we’ll include an expectation table — cold-start window is expected to add ~40–60 ms at the 99th pctl for sequence lengths near ~120 tokens (depends on model binding). We’ll run a cold-start experiment during Phase A and capture results.
- Cost assumptions: the $0.0015/token assumes batching at avg batch size 6–8, KV-cache hit rate ~25% on prompt prefixes, and quantized model variant (int8) where applicable. The appendix spells this out.
- Soak plan: default is 1-hour at target concurrency; we can also run a 4x 15-minute consecutive run if you prefer.

I’ve attached: poc-playbook-v1.pdf (with appendix) and workload-sample.jsonl. Monica will stand up the sandbox cluster Monday and send credentials.

—Ben
Principal Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
